question: Can a caller-owned Claude MCP server named harness-tools retain its identity and stream events after per-harness mcpServers became public?

sources.name: Vercel AI SDK Claude Code bridge MCP merge
sources.claim: External mcpServers are copied by caller key; when host AI SDK tools exist the bridge assigns its internal MCP server to mcpServers['harness-tools'], replacing any caller server under that key.

sources.name: Vercel AI SDK Claude stream translator
sources.claim: Every mcp__harness-tools__ tool-use id is classified as internal host-tool transport and its native tool-call/result events are suppressed; other mcp__ tools are emitted as dynamic external MCP tools.

sources.name: Vercel AI SDK harness MCP server API
sources.claim: The public mcpServers setting accepts MCP server definitions keyed by server name and does not document harness-tools as a reserved caller name.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: An ordinary external server name such as context7 remains dynamic and visible.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The model recognizes the normal new MCP path as a negative control.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: An external harness-tools server remains configured without host tools but its events are classified as internal and suppressed.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: Name-prefix identity alone causes the external server's stream to disappear.

distinguishing_outcomes.observation: When host tools are present, the internal harness-tools server overwrites the caller server under the same key.
distinguishing_outcomes.interpretation: The same undocumented name collision changes from stream misclassification to configuration replacement.

stop_condition: Stop after current-main source, one ordinary-name negative control, one executable collision model, and a target-native stream discriminator establish the server-name identity issue.
